drafts.title: Business case: procurement outcomes and delivery economics
actions: Reconcile a sample of completed orders from customer request through delivery and settlement.

tasks.action: Reconcile a sample of completed orders from customer request through delivery and settlement.
tasks.deliverable: Order-level findings: repeat demand, delivery reliability, contribution and cash exposure.
required_inputs: Anonymized order and invoice records with payment dates, delivery timestamps, refunds and staff time
tasks.success_measure: Each sampled order reconciles to invoices and delivery records; report unresolved amounts and exceptions rather than treating them as zero.

unknowns: Anonymized order and invoice records with payment dates, delivery timestamps, refunds and staff time

sections.heading: What the evidence supports
sections.content: Waybill describes sourcing parts, comparing quotes, routing approval and payment, managing freight/customs, and updating inventory. The buyer problem is coordinating a purchase across suppliers and intermediaries. This suggests evaluating it as a procurement and fulfillment service with automation, rather than assuming pure software economics. These are company descriptions, not verified delivery outcomes.

sections.heading: What could make this an expensive service business
sections.content: The important risk is that supplier exceptions, customs delays, fallback sourcing and human coordination consume the fee. A large order value can hide a small or negative service contribution. Reconcile recognized revenue and direct delivery costs under a consistent gross/net treatment; separately measure cash paid to suppliers before cash collected from customers. The site describes a fallback source, but does not establish its reliability or cost in real orders.

sections.heading: The decisive evidence gap
sections.content: No comparable dated revenue or paying-customer figures were found in the collected sources. Website demonstrations of faster procurement are not company growth. Ask for anonymized completed-order records: request date, promised/actual delivery, customer invoice, supplier/freight/duty costs, refunds, staff time and payment dates. Repeat paid orders and contribution per order would change the incubation decision more than another product description.

drafts.decision: Worth a bounded commercial test with hardware teams facing urgent component purchases. The evidence supports the product proposition; it does not yet establish repeat paid demand or profitable fulfillment.

drafts.title: GTM: a paid critical-component procurement pilot
actions: Agree and run a bounded paid procurement pilot with one qualified hardware buyer.

tasks.action: Agree and run a bounded paid procurement pilot with one qualified hardware buyer.
tasks.deliverable: A pilot scorecard with paid demand, delivery outcomes, repeat-order intent and order contribution.
required_inputs: A consenting buyer, comparable baseline orders, approved scope/pricing and delivery-cost records
tasks.success_measure: Proceed only with payment, repeat-order demand, agreed delivery performance and positive contribution; investigate or stop when these conditions fail.

unknowns: A consenting buyer, comparable baseline orders, approved scope/pricing and delivery-cost records

sections.heading: Buyer, trigger and initial wedge · hypothesis
sections.content: Proposed user: the engineer specifying the component. Proposed buyer: the procurement or operations lead; finance approves the order. Target teams with a current bill of materials, a firm delivery date and repeated coordination work. A prototype or production deadline is a stronger trigger than general interest in AI. Begin with a narrow component purchase that has a measurable existing process.

sections.heading: Acquisition and offer · proposed
sections.content: Build a prospect list from public hardware accelerator portfolios and manufacturing associations, then qualify teams with an immediate component requirement. These are proposed channels, not established partnerships. Draft offer: “Give us one component requirement, quantity and need-by date. We will propose a landed-cost quote, sourcing fallback and delivery plan for a paid pilot.” Agree scope, fees, exceptions and responsibility before the order. No outreach has been sent.

sections.heading: Bounded pilot and decision rule · proposed
sections.content: Proposed first test: one consenting buyer and a small set of orders over 30 days; scope and pricing must be agreed. Measure on-time delivered commitments divided by all commitments due, and request-to-delivery time against comparable previous orders. Record every failed order. Calculate contribution after direct fulfillment and human effort, keeping supplier pass-through treatment consistent. Continue only if the buyer pays, requests another order, delivery performance meets the agreed baseline and contribution is positive. A small pilot tests feasibility; it does not establish market-wide demand.

drafts.decision: Start with small hardware teams buying time-critical components. Sell a bounded procurement outcome to the operations or procurement lead, with finance approving the spend. This is a proposed segment to test.

drafts.title: Investor narrative · internal starting draft
actions: Complete the narrative with reconciled commercial records and an explicit financing plan.

tasks.action: Complete the narrative with reconciled commercial records and an explicit financing plan.
tasks.deliverable: A cited investor narrative with an operating evidence table and unresolved figures clearly marked.
required_inputs: Company financials, order cohorts, authorized customer evidence, current cash/burn and proposed raise parameters
tasks.success_measure: Material claims and figures are substantiated and reviewed before investor release.

unknowns: Company financials, order cohorts, authorized customer evidence, current cash/burn and proposed raise parameters

sections.heading: Company and customer problem · source claims
sections.content: Hardware teams can coordinate procurement across distributors, approvals, payments, freight and customs. Waybill describes a service that takes a part specification or bill of materials and manages that sequence through delivery and inventory updates. Its proposed value is fewer coordination steps and more predictable component availability. Public product descriptions support this positioning, but not measured savings or customer adoption.

sections.heading: Commercial thesis and risk · hypothesis
sections.content: The commercial hypothesis is that teams with repeated urgent component needs will pay for reliable procurement and return for subsequent orders. The thesis strengthens if automation reduces the human effort required per completed order while delivery reliability holds. It weakens if supplier exceptions and service work grow as fast as order volume, or if customers value the service but will not pay enough to cover delivery costs.

sections.heading: Traction and financing placeholders
sections.content: Collected sources do not establish annual revenue growth, active paying customers, repeat-order rate, contribution margin, cash conversion or current runway. These fields remain unknown. The next version needs an order-level operating table, customer references where authorized, financial records and a use-of-funds schedule. Separate product development needs from any working-capital requirement. This identified narrative is an internal draft, not an approved anonymized teaser or investor release.

drafts.decision: The product and proposed commercial thesis can be described. Traction, market size, revenue quality, raise amount and valuation cannot yet be substantiated from the collected evidence.

drafts.title: Fundraising readiness: prove repeatable order economics
actions: Prepare a financing evidence brief connecting an order cohort, operating milestone and monthly cash requirement.

tasks.action: Prepare a financing evidence brief connecting an order cohort, operating milestone and monthly cash requirement.
tasks.deliverable: A readiness brief and conditional mandate shortlist criteria supported by operating records.
required_inputs: Paid-order cohorts, fulfillment costs, customer/supplier payment dates, cash/burn and desired financing parameters
tasks.success_measure: The operating evidence answers the scalability objection and the capital requirement reconciles to a measurable milestone.

unknowns: Paid-order cohorts, fulfillment costs, customer/supplier payment dates, cash/burn and desired financing parameters

sections.heading: Likely investor objection and proof milestone · analysis
sections.content: The likely objection is whether this is a scalable automated service or a coordination-heavy business whose costs rise with each order. The useful milestone is a paid order cohort showing repeat purchases, on-time delivery, recorded staff effort and contribution after fulfillment costs. Supplier and authenticity checks matter, but repeating the website’s sourcing promise is not proof that those checks work.

sections.heading: Investor mandate fit · hypothesis
sections.content: Potential mandate types include early-stage investors in supply-chain technology, industrial workflows and automation-enabled business services. Evaluate actual mandates, geographic scope, stage, check size and portfolio conflicts before naming matches. Funds requiring demonstrated recurring software revenue may need evidence that service fees, repeat usage and margins fit their mandate. No named investor or investment eligibility has been verified.

sections.heading: Capital need and sequence · proposed
sections.content: First establish the operating baseline and cash timing. Then distinguish spending on product automation, supplier/fulfillment capabilities and customer acquisition from cash required to bridge customer and supplier payments. Prepare a monthly use-of-funds and cash schedule tied to a measurable operating milestone. Raise size, instrument, runway and valuation remain unknown; they should not be inferred from the product’s ambition or accelerator membership.

drafts.decision: Prioritize repeat paid demand and contribution per order before positioning this as scalable procurement infrastructure. A pre-revenue raise may still be possible, but the public evidence cannot establish the right stage, amount or valuation.

research.business: Waybill is an agentic procurement and inventory management platform for hardware and deep-tech teams.
research.reason_to_meet: The business opportunity lies in simplifying the procurement process for hardware teams, which currently takes weeks and involves multiple steps and parties. Waybill automates this process, potentially saving time and reducing errors.
research.main_risk: The main risk is that delivery/service costs could exceed the fees paid by customers, especially if the costs of sourcing, negotiation, freight, customs, and delivery are higher than anticipated.
research.first_question: Can you provide an example of a successful procurement process managed by Waybill that resulted in cost savings for a customer?

pitch.subject: A prospect shortlist for Waybill
pitch.observation: Your public update asks for introductions to procurement leads at hardware enterprises.
pitch.proposed_help: We could build a researched shortlist of relevant organizations and decision-maker roles, explain why each fits your target, and draft personalized outreach for your review. We would first agree the target profile with you; introductions and meetings are not guaranteed.

priorities.title: Establish paid customer demand
priorities.investor_question: How many customers are using Waybill for procurement?
priorities.action: Analyze Waybill's booking/order/payment records to determine actual customer count
priorities.output: A record of the number of customers using Waybill for procurement
priorities.done_when: Show paid purchases and repeat business for a dated customer group, including cancellations and refunds. If no sales exist, record that gap and propose a paid test.

priorities.title: Check what each sale earns
priorities.investor_question: After direct delivery costs, how much does the company keep from each sale?
priorities.action: Compare Waybill's fees collected from customers with its direct fulfillment and staff costs, including payment timing
priorities.output: A table of customer receipts, recognized revenue, direct delivery costs and payment dates.
priorities.done_when: Show contribution per completed sale, unpaid balances and any negative results. Contribution excludes overhead; it is not total company profit.

priorities.action: Compile a summary of Waybill's demand, economics, and next milestone based on sourced evidence

priorities.done_when: Link each business claim to its source. Show what is proven, what is still unknown and the next milestone that funding would support.
